deities: Jogeshwari Devi (Bhagwati; presiding deity, worshipped as a self-manifested goddess and described by the temple institution as a subsidiary Shakti Peetha)

history.period: Ancient rock-cut cave shrine; exact construction date unknown (verify)
history.summary: IMPORTANT IDENTITY NOTE: This record is mapped provisionally to the Shri Jogeshwari Devi rock-cut cave temple at Ghatnandra village, Sillod taluka, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district - the best-documented Jogeshwari temple in the district with its own official website (jogeshwaridevi.org). Other Jogeshwari temples exist in the region, including a Jogeshwari temple in Jogeshwari village (Paithan area, PIN 431105), listings near Uttar Jayakwadi/Katpur (Paithan), and a city-area 'Jogeshwri Devi Maa Temple' in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar; a Temples of India listing gives an ambiguous address 'Jogeshwari, Maharashtra 431133'. The CSV identity cannot be definitively pinned to one of these, so this file should be treated as provisional (verify). About the Ghatnandra temple: it is an ancient rock-cut cave shrine carved into a hill of the Ajanta range on the Khandesh-Marathwada boundary, about 4.5 km from Ghatnandra village. The temple's own tradition holds that Bhagwati Jogeshwari Devi is a self-manifested (swayambhu) goddess and a subsidiary Shakti Peetha - a religious claim, not an established historical fact. No dynasty, patron, or construction date is verifiably documented for the cave (verify). Recorded administration: the temple was under the charge of the local tehsildar from about 1967 to 1998, and has since been managed by a registered temple board (Shri Jogeshwari Devi Sansthan, registered 1999). Navratri brings the largest gatherings; an annual jatra/fair is held in the temple's grounds. A 'Chaturdashi' observance is also noted in the institution's festival calendar.

name: Jogeshwari Temple
town_description: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad), in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra, is a historic city famed as the gateway to the UNESCO World Heritage sites of Ajanta and Ellora caves, the Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga, and the 17th-century Bibi Ka Maqbara. The temple in this record is not in the city itself but near Ghatnandra village in Sillod taluka of the same district (village code 431113; PIN 431113 on the official temple website) - about 30 km from Sillod town and roughly 70-90 km from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar city (distances vary by source, verify). Ghatnandra sits on the Khandesh-Marathwada boundary in the Ajanta hill range and is also known for the Manu Devi waterfall nearby.

travel.airport: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Airport (IXU), formerly Aurangabad Airport, approx. 70-90 km (verify); the next alternative is Jalgaon Airport (verify).
travel.railway: Nearest major railway junction: Pachora Junction, approx. 35 km from Ghatnandra (per a local source; verify); Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Railway Station (AWB) is approx. 70 km and better connected. Sillod town itself has no railway station (verify).
travel.road: Approx. 30 km from Sillod tehsil headquarters and approx. 70 km from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar city via Sillod (local source; the temple's own site says approx. 90 km north of the city - verify exact distance). The temple hill is about 4.5 km from Ghatnandra village. Reachable by private taxi/cab or state transport buses to Sillod/Ghatnandra, then local transport. Expect a climb up the hill to the cave shrine.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when Marathwada's weather is coolest. Navratri (September-October) is the most spiritually significant period with the largest crowds and fair; monsoon visits offer lush surroundings but slippery cave/hill paths (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not reliably published; confirm with the temple before visiting (verify). Like most Maharashtra hill shrines, darshan is likely from early morning to evening; the temple phone listed on official sources is +91-9923014667 (verify).
